source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Ecology and Environment
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: The functional role of a species in its habitat is its
questions.explanation: Habitat is the address; niche is the profession — the range of conditions and resources a species uses.

questions.stem: Natality of a population refers to the
questions.explanation: Natality is births (or hatching) per unit time; mortality is deaths; immigration and emigration are movements.

questions.stem: In logistic growth, the maximum population size that the environment can support is the
questions.explanation: The S-shaped curve levels off at K, the carrying capacity of that habitat.

questions.stem: An interaction in which both species benefit, such as mycorrhiza or lichen, is
questions.explanation: Mutualism is +/+ ; predation and parasitism are +/- ; competition is -/- ; amensalism is -/0.

questions.stem: Gross primary productivity of an ecosystem is the rate of
options: energy lost as heat by consumers
organic matter produced by photosynthesis including that used in plant respiration
questions.explanation: GPP is total photosynthesis; NPP = GPP − respiratory loss of producers, and is available to consumers.

questions.stem: In a grazing food chain the first trophic level is always occupied by
questions.explanation: Autotrophs fix energy; herbivores are primary consumers at the second trophic level.

questions.stem: The pyramid of energy in a natural ecosystem is always
questions.explanation: Energy is lost as heat at each transfer (about 10% rule), so the energy pyramid cannot invert.

questions.stem: Protection of species in their natural habitat, as in a national park, is
questions.explanation: In-situ keeps organisms in the ecosystem; zoos, seed banks and botanical gardens are ex-situ.

questions.stem: A high BOD of a water sample indicates
options: a large amount of organic waste and high microbial oxygen use
questions.explanation: Biochemical oxygen demand rises when microbes oxidise sewage; fish may die from oxygen depletion.

questions.stem: The principal greenhouse gas released by burning fossil fuels is
questions.explanation: CO2, along with methane, N2O and CFCs, traps outgoing infrared radiation and warms the troposphere.

questions.stem: An expanding population has an age pyramid that is
options: triangular with a broad base of pre-reproductive individuals
questions.explanation: A wide base means many children; a stable population is bell-shaped; a declining one is urn-shaped.

questions.stem: Competitive exclusion (Gause's principle) states that two species with identical niches
options: cannot occupy the same habitat indefinitely
questions.explanation: Complete competitors cannot coexist; one is eliminated or they partition resources.

questions.stem: Which statement about ozone and greenhouse gases is incorrect?
options: CFCs release chlorine that catalytically destroys ozone
The ozone hole is most pronounced over Antarctica in spring
Ground-level ozone from CFCs is the main UV shield for humans
questions.explanation: Beneficial ozone is in the stratosphere; tropospheric ozone is a pollutant. CFCs destroy stratospheric O3, they do not create a UV shield at ground level.

questions.stem: Among the following, the most specific description of where an organism lives is its
questions.explanation: Habitat is the place with a particular set of abiotic and biotic conditions occupied by the organism.

questions.stem: Immigration increases a population's size while emigration
questions.explanation: N_{t+1} = N_t + (B + I) − (D + E); emigration removes individuals.

questions.stem: Exponential (geometric) growth produces a curve that is
options: J-shaped when resources are not limiting
questions.explanation: dN/dt = rN gives a J-curve; logistic growth adds (K−N)/K and becomes sigmoid.

questions.stem: Commensalism is an interaction in which
options: one benefits and the other is unaffected
questions.explanation: Example: orchid on a mango tree, or cattle egret with grazing cattle (+/0).

questions.stem: Net primary productivity is
options: GPP minus respiratory losses of autotrophs
questions.explanation: NPP is the energy stored as producer biomass and available to the rest of the food chain.

questions.stem: A detritus food chain begins with
questions.explanation: Decomposers and detritivores feed on dead remains; grazing chains start with living producers.

questions.stem: A pyramid of biomass may be inverted in a
options: grassland with grasses heavier than herbivores
aquatic system where phytoplankton biomass is less than that of zooplankton at a given time
pyramid of energy of any ecosystem
questions.explanation: Phytoplankton turn over so fast that standing crop is small, so biomass pyramid can invert; energy pyramid never does.

questions.stem: Sacred groves in India are examples of
options: in-situ conservation by traditional protection of forest patches
questions.explanation: Community-protected groves shelter many rare plants and animals in their native habitat.

questions.stem: Eutrophication of lakes is accelerated mainly by
options: addition of nitrates and phosphates from sewage and fertilisers
questions.explanation: Nutrient enrichment causes algal blooms; their decay raises BOD and can kill fish.

questions.stem: Good ozone that filters ultraviolet radiation is concentrated in the
questions.explanation: The stratospheric ozone layer absorbs UV-B; tropospheric ozone is a component of photochemical smog.

questions.stem: According to Lindeman, the efficiency of energy transfer between two successive trophic levels is of the order of
options: 1% from sun to all levels equally
questions.explanation: Roughly one-tenth of the energy at one level is converted to biomass at the next (10% law).

questions.stem: Hotspots of biodiversity are regions with
options: high endemism that are under severe habitat loss
questions.explanation: Myers' hotspots combine exceptional endemic species richness with serious threat, e.g. Western Ghats.

questions.stem: Which statement about climate treaties and greenhouse gases is incorrect?
options: Montreal Protocol aims to phase out ozone-depleting substances
Kyoto Protocol addressed greenhouse gas emissions
UV-B can cause snow blindness and skin cancers
Methane is not a greenhouse gas
questions.explanation: Methane is a potent greenhouse gas from wetlands, cattle and rice fields; CO2 is the most abundant anthropogenic one.
